limitations: The displayed inverse-distance and inverse-tour-length expressions require positive finite distances and tour lengths. Probability normalization needs finite nonnegative weights with a positive total. Zero pheromone, underflow or infeasible candidates require explicit handling.

Setting alpha=0 removes pheromone dependence; it leaves heuristic-weighted random selection, not a deterministic nearest-neighbor rule. Equal initial pheromone likewise does not imply uniform selection when heuristic values differ.

claims.statement: In the inspected positive-distance traveling-salesman formulation, place m ants at starting cities and initialize pheromone trails. An ant at city i samples an unvisited city j with probability proportional to tau_ij^alpha * eta_ij^beta, where eta_ij=1/d_ij; normalize over the currently unvisited cities. Each ant stores its visited cities and returns to its start after visiting every city. After all tours are complete, the ant-cycle rule updates every trail as tau_ij_new=rho*tau_ij+sum_k delta_tau_ij_k, with delta_tau_ij_k=Q/L_k if ant k used that edge and zero otherwise. Here rho is retention, 1−rho is evaporation, and L_k is the completed tour length. Reset tour-specific visited lists and deposit accumulators for the next iteration while retaining the best tour found. Ant-density instead deposits a constant Q per traversed edge at each step; ant-quantity deposits Q/d_ij per step. Those variants do not use the ant-cycle complete-tour deposit.

entries.name: Ant Colony System
entries.definition: An ant-colony optimization algorithm that combines a greedy-or-proportional construction rule, local pheromone updates during construction, and global pheromone updates restricted to a selected best tour.
entries.identity_notes: The selected baseline is the paper’s global-best ACS with local interpolation toward the initial trail tau0. It is distinct from Ant System’s all-ant deposits, MAX–MIN trail clipping, and the Ant-Q variant whose local target uses a discounted maximum future trail. Iteration-best reinforcement and ACS with local search are explicitly described variants, not silently incorporated into the baseline. No normalized identity match was found across all 442 pinned AIO labels/scoped synonyms and 288 preceding native IDs/names/aliases. Full-checkout fixed-string searches included ignored and hidden files in worktree and main, returning 10 and 10 lines respectively. Every text hit was a prior candidate lead. Six exact AIO CLASS nodes with scoped synonyms/comments and outgoing edges and five native neighboring mechanisms were inspected. Absence is bounded to this snapshot and semantic neighborhood.
limitations: The local update moves a trail toward tau0: it decreases a trail only when that trail exceeds tau0, increases it below tau0, and leaves equality unchanged. It is not unconditional evaporation. At q0=1 the displayed decision uses only maximization, apart from tie handling, so positive trails alone do not supply probabilistic exploration.

There is a source presentation ambiguity: Equation 4 defines zero deposit off the best tour, while Section III explicitly restricts the global update to best-tour edges. Appendix A’s global loop uses stale ant-indexed endpoints inside a generic edge loop, and its repeat jump does not explicitly reset all tour state. The record follows the main-text scope and supplies the necessary state-reset qualification; it does not claim the appendix is directly executable or that an official erratum was checked.

Random initial cities, heuristic powers, q0, alpha, rho and tau0 are configuration choices. Repeated local updates and their ordering affect trails; independent construction of entire tours is not an equivalent schedule. Zero distances, zero denominators, constraints and numerical underflow need handling.

The paper’s task-specific comparisons, optional local search and qualitative improvement claims do not establish universal superiority or finite-run global optimality. Ant-Q’s reinforcement-learning connection does not make the selected tau0 rule a Bellman update.

claims.statement: For a traveling-salesman tour, at each construction decision draw q uniformly in [0,1]. If q<=q0, choose an unvisited city maximizing tau_ij*eta_ij^beta; otherwise sample proportionally to those same weights over the unvisited set. Apply the selected local rule tau_ij_new=(1−rho)*tau_ij+rho*tau0 to traversed edges during construction. After all tours finish, update edges belonging to the shortest tour found so far with tau_ij_new=(1−alpha)*tau_ij+alpha/L_best. The scope of this global step follows Section III’s explicit best-tour-edge restriction; edges outside that tour do not undergo this global update. Figure 3 organizes construction into steps. Appendix A has all ants choose a step before its local-update loop, so sequential whole-tour construction is not assumed. Retain the best-so-far tour and reset per-tour feasibility state before the next iteration. Parameter settings, tie handling and repeated updates to an edge must be declared for an executable implementation.

entries.definition: An ant-colony optimization algorithm that reinforces solution components from a single selected best ant per iteration, constrains pheromone trails between lower and upper limits, and initializes trails high to encourage early exploration.
entries.identity_notes: This record denotes MAX–MIN Ant System as described in the inspected 1999 author preprint associated with the 2000 journal article. It retains the defining bounded-trail and single-best reinforcement mechanism. Iteration-best, global-best and mixed schedules are specified choices; local search, candidate lists and pheromone smoothing are optional configurations. It is not the unbounded all-ant Ant System update or the selected ACS greedy/local-update rule. No normalized identity match was found across all 442 pinned AIO labels/scoped synonyms and 288 preceding native IDs/names/aliases. Full-checkout fixed-string searches included ignored and hidden files in worktree and main, returning 10 and 10 lines respectively. Every text hit was a prior candidate lead. limitations: Positive lower trails provide nonzero probabilities only for choices that remain eligible and have positive finite heuristic weights with a finite positive normalizer. The paper’s optional nearest-neighbor candidate lists exclude otherwise feasible choices, and its fallback is deterministic maximization; positive bounds therefore do not prove full tour support for that implementation.

The p_best lower-limit heuristic assumes the simplified TSP branching model, alpha=1 and negligible heuristic differences; changing the pheromone exponent changes the displayed probability relation. Choosing p_best=1 yields tau_min=0 in the displayed formula, which does not satisfy a strict positive-bound premise. Small n, changing branch counts and numerical underflow require additional configuration decisions.

The geometric-series argument bounds a recurrence under a maximum deposit. That argument alone does not establish that every changing trail sequence has a limit, nor that a finite run reaches the global optimum. The source’s trail-bound notion of convergence must not be equated with optimality or all ants taking the same tour.

Equal high pheromone does not imply uniform construction when heuristic weights differ. Best-so-far reinforcement, iteration-best mixing, candidate lists, local search, smoothing and restart rules affect behavior and must be declared. The reported TSP/QAP comparisons are not reproduced and no universal performance guarantee is asserted.

claims.statement: Construct solutions by choosing feasible components with probabilities proportional to tau^alpha*eta^beta, as in Ant System. For positive-cost minimization, select one iteration-best or best-so-far solution according to the declared reinforcement schedule. Evaporate every trail using retention rho and add 1/f(best) only to components of that selected solution, with zero deposit elsewhere. Clip the resulting trails to [tau_min,tau_max] after each iteration. The source initializes trails at a high value that is brought to the upper limit; this preserves initial exploration pressure relative to low trails. Its upper-limit estimate is tau_max=1/((1−rho)*f(best_so_far)), updated when the best cost improves. For the source’s TSP lower-limit heuristic, n is the number of cities and avg=n/2 approximates the number of choices at each step. The displayed formula uses unit pheromone exponent alpha=1, equal decision probabilities and negligible heuristic differences: with p_dec=p_best^(1/n), tau_min=tau_max*(1−p_dec)/((avg−1)*p_dec), capped at tau_max if larger. This is an approximate configuration rule, not the exact probability of reconstructing a real tour. Positive limits, 0<=rho<1, a valid denominator and declared handling of boundary parameters are required for this account.

native_neighbors.name: Differential Evolution
native_neighbors.definition: A population-based continuous optimization method that generates trial vectors using scaled differences between population members, combines mutant and target coordinates, and selects replacements through target-trial objective comparisons.
native_neighbors.identity_notes: This record denotes differential evolution, with the 1997 DE/rand/1/bin procedure as its explicitly inspected core. Mutation/crossover variants are distinguished by the source’s DE/x/y/z notation rather than treated as identical executable rules. It differs from generic genetic algorithms, a fitted Gaussian search distribution, objective-gradient descent, and DEHB’s additional budget-specific populations and Hyperband scheduling. No normalized identity match was found across all 442 pinned AIO labels/scoped synonyms and 270 preceding native IDs/names/aliases. Full-checkout fixed-string searches included ignored and hidden files in worktree and main, returning 19 and 19 lines respectively. These were prior candidate leads, source discussions and neighboring DEHB/FABOLAS method mentions. Eight exact AIO CLASS nodes with scoped synonyms and outgoing edges and seven native neighboring mechanisms were inspected. Absence is bounded to this snapshot and semantic neighborhood.
limitations: The prose specifies replacement for a strictly smaller objective, whereas the displayed C-style Figure3 uses <=. The tie policy must therefore be identified when implementing or comparing versions; these source statements are not treated as identical code. A forced mutant coordinate need not change its numerical value.

DE/rand/1/bin needs at least four population members for its distinct-index rule. Difference-vector proposals can leave the initialization range; that range is not a hard feasible-domain boundary. Bound repair, general constraint handling, noise treatment and categorical encodings are additional choices.

The method uses function evaluations, not derivatives of the objective. Population collapse can eliminate difference-vector variation, and finite-budget greedy selection does not certify a global optimum. The source’s control-variable suggestions and comparative results are empirical, not universal guarantees or reproduced experiments.

claims.statement: Maintain a fixed-size population of real-valued vectors. In the inspected DE/rand/1/bin scheme, for each target select three mutually distinct current-generation population indices that also differ from the target index. Add a scaled difference of two selected vectors to the third to form a mutant. Build a trial by independently choosing mutant or target coordinates according to the crossover probability, forcing one randomly selected coordinate to come from the mutant. Evaluate the trial and use a greedy comparison against its target to choose the next-generation member. Complete all target comparisons using the old population before replacing it with the next population. Repeat until the configured stopping criterion is met. Population size, mutation scale, crossover probability and initialization are configuration choices.

native_neighbors.definition: A stochastic optimization procedure that explores candidate configurations with temperature-controlled acceptance of cost-increasing moves and progressively cools that acceptance process to concentrate search on low-cost configurations.
native_neighbors.identity_notes: This record denotes the temperature-scheduled optimization procedure exemplified by Kirkpatrick, Gelatt and Vecchi. The 1983 article is a primary formulation, not a claim of exclusive invention. limitations: The exp(−delta/T) expression is for positive effective temperature with the physical Boltzmann constant absorbed into its cost units. Zero temperature is a limiting or separately defined greedy rule, not evaluation of that quotient at T=0. Equal-cost moves are accepted in the displayed symmetric-proposal rule.

At fixed T the Boltzmann interpretation requires a proper target and a valid transition construction. Arbitrary asymmetric proposals do not justify dropping the reverse-to-forward proposal ratio. Lowering T changes the target; stationarity for a fixed stage does not imply equilibrium throughout a finite cooling run.

Positive-temperature uphill acceptance only permits escape through moves supported by the proposal. It does not ensure reaching every state, escaping a local basin in a chosen budget or tracking equilibrium. Rapid cooling can freeze search prematurely; schedule length, cost scale, move connectivity and constraints matter.

The primary article’s heuristics and empirical scaling claims are not a finite-run global-convergence theorem or a universal complexity bound. The later mathematical conditions for asymptotic annealing convergence were not audited here. No electronic-design or traveling-salesman benchmark is reproduced.

limitations: A score>=threshold rule need not select exactly rho*N candidates: order-statistic indexing and tied scores can increase the elite count. Implementations must state their quantile, tie and optimization-direction conventions; minimization requires the corresponding lower-score criterion or an equivalent score transformation.

Unsmoothed finite-sample fitting can produce Bernoulli probabilities 0 or 1 and remove future exploration. Interior initialization and 0<alpha<1 prevent exact endpoints after a single convex smoothing step in exact arithmetic; smoothing alone does not guarantee exploration forever or a global optimum, and finite precision can still collapse support.
